sanskrit: tataḥ prāvartata punaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ kaṭukodayaḥ rāmarāvaṇasainyānām anyonyam abhidhāvatām
english: Then the battle broke out again, bitter and fierce, as the armies of Rāma and Rāvaṇa charged at one another.

sanskrit: śataśo nairṛtān vanyā jaghnur vanyāṃś ca nairṛtāḥ nairṛtās tatra vadhyante prāyaśo na tu vānarāḥ
english: The forest-dwellers slew the demons by the hundreds, and the demons slew the forest-dwellers in turn; yet in that place it was the demons who were chiefly slain, and not the monkeys.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ śrutvā hataṃ saṃkhye kumbhakarṇaṃ sahānugam prahastaṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ dhūmrākṣaṃ cātitejasam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, upon hearing that Kumbhakarṇa together with his followers had been slain in battle, and also the great archer Prahasta, and the exceedingly fierce Dhūmrākṣa,

sanskrit: putram indrajitaṃ śūraṃ rāvaṇaḥ pratyabhāṣata jahi rāmam amitraghna sugrīvaṃ ca salakṣmaṇam
english: Rāvaṇa addressed his valiant son Indrajit: "O slayer of enemies, kill Rāma, and Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tvayā hi mama satputra yaśo dīptam upārjitam jitvā vajradharaṃ saṃkhye sahasrākṣaṃ śacīpatim
english: "For it is by you, O good son, that blazing glory has been won for me — by conquering in battle the bearer of the thunderbolt, the thousand-eyed lord of Śacī."

sanskrit: antarhitaḥ prakāśo vā divyair dattavaraiḥ śaraiḥ jahi śatrūn amitraghna mama śastrabhṛtāṃ vara
english: "Whether hidden or visible, with your divine arrows whose boons have been granted, slay our enemies, O destroyer of foes, O best among those who bear weapons for my sake."

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇasugrīvāḥ śarasparśaṃ na te 'nagha samarthāḥ pratisaṃsoḍhuṃ kutas tadanuyāyinaḥ
english: "Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva are not capable of enduring the touch of your arrows, O sinless one — how much less, then, their followers?"

sanskrit: akṛtā yā prahastena kumbhakarṇena cānagha kharasyāpacitiḥ saṃkhye tāṃ gacchasva mahābhuja
english: "The vengeance for Khara that was left unaccomplished by Prahasta and Kumbhakarṇa in battle — go and accomplish that, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: tvam adya niśitair bāṇair hatvā śatrūn sasainikān pratinandaya māṃ putra purā baddhveva vāsavam
english: "Today, having slain the enemies together with their forces by your sharp arrows, delight me, my son, as you once did by binding Vāsava himself."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tathety uktvā ratham āsthāya daṃśitaḥ prayayāv indrajid rājaṃs tūrṇam āyodhanaṃ prati
english: Thus addressed, Indrajit replied "So be it," and clad in armour, mounting his chariot, he quickly set out toward the battlefield, O king.

sanskrit: tatra viśrāvya vispaṣṭaṃ nāma rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ āhvayām āsa samare lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam
english: There that foremost of rakshasas, having announced his name clearly, challenged Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks to combat.

sanskrit: taṃ lakṣmaṇo 'py abhyadhāvat pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ trāsayaṃs talaghoṣeṇa siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: Lakṣmaṇa too rushed at him, grasping his arrow-strung bow, terrifying him with the slap of his palm, as a lion intimidates a lesser beast.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ sumahaj jayagṛddhinoḥ divyāstraviduṣos tīvram anyonyaspardhinos tadā
english: Between those two, eager for victory, both versed in divine weapons, a mighty and fierce battle arose, each striving to outdo the other.

sanskrit: rāvaṇis tu yadā nainaṃ viśeṣayati sāyakaiḥ tato gurutaraṃ yatnam ātiṣṭhad balināṃ varaḥ
english: When Rāvaṇa's son could not gain the upper hand over him with arrows, that best of the mighty redoubled his effort.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ mahāvegair ardayām āsa tomaraiḥ tān āgatān sa ciccheda saumitrir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ te nikṛttāḥ śarais tīkṣṇair nyapatan vasudhātale
english: Then he assailed him with javelins of great speed; but Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, cut them down with sharp arrows. Severed by the keen arrows, they fell upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tam aṅgado vālisutaḥ śrīmān udyamya pādapam abhidrutya mahāvegas tāḍayām āsa mūrdhani
english: Then the glorious Aṅgada, son of Vālī, swift as the wind, snatched up a tree and rushing forward struck him on the head.

sanskrit: tasyendrajid asaṃbhrāntaḥ prāsenorasi vīryavān prahartum aicchat taṃ cāsya prāsaṃ ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Unshaken, the valiant Indrajit wished to strike him on the chest with a spear; but Lakṣmaṇa cut that spear of his to pieces.

sanskrit: tam abhyāśagataṃ vīram aṅgadaṃ rāvaṇātmajaḥ gadayātāḍayat savye pārśve vānarapuṃgavam
english: The son of Rāvaṇa then struck that hero Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, who had come close, with his mace on the left flank.

sanskrit: tam acintya prahāraṃ sa balavān vālinaḥ sutaḥ sasarjendrajitaḥ krodhāc chālaskandham amitrajit
english: That powerful son of Vālī, the slayer of enemies, paying no heed to the blow, hurled in fury at Indrajit the trunk of a shala tree.

sanskrit: so 'ṅgadena ruṣotsṛṣṭo vadhāyendrajitas taruḥ jaghānendrajitaḥ pārtha rathaṃ sāśvaṃ sasārathim
english: That tree, hurled in wrath by Aṅgada to destroy Indrajit, O Pārtha, smashed Indrajit's chariot together with its horses and charioteer.

sanskrit: tato hatāśvāt praskandya rathāt sa hatasārathiḥ tatraivāntardadhe rājan māyayā rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: Then, leaping down from the chariot whose horses had been slain, his charioteer killed, that son of Rāvaṇa vanished on that very spot through his power of illusion, O king.

sanskrit: antarhitaṃ viditvā taṃ bahumāyaṃ ca rākṣasam rāmas taṃ deśam āgamya tat sainyaṃ paryarakṣata
english: Knowing that the demon possessed of many illusions had become invisible, Rāma came to that place and stood guard over his army.

sanskrit: sa rāmam uddiśya śarais tato dattavarais tadā vivyādha sarvagātreṣu lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham
english: Then, aiming at Rāma with his boon-given arrows, he pierced him all over his limbs, and likewise the great warrior Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tam adṛśyaṃ śaraiḥ śūrau māyayāntarhitaṃ tadā yodhayām āsatur ubhau rāvaṇiṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Both heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, fought against that Rāvaṇa's son who was hidden by illusion and invisible, shooting arrows at him.

sanskrit: sa ruṣā sarvagātreṣu tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ vyasṛjat sāyakān bhūyaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: He, in fury, released arrows upon every limb of those two lion-men, again and again, by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: tam adṛśyaṃ vicinvantaḥ sṛjantam aniśaṃ śarān harayo viviśur vyoma pragṛhya mahatīḥ śilāḥ
english: Seeking him who was invisible yet ceaselessly releasing arrows, the monkeys entered the sky grasping great boulders.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca tau cāpy adṛśyaḥ sa śarair vivyādha rākṣasaḥ sa bhṛśaṃ tāḍayan vīro rāvaṇir māyayāvṛtaḥ
english: And those two as well as all the monkeys — the invisible demon pierced with arrows; that hero, the son of Rāvaṇa, veiled by illusion, struck them violently.

sanskrit: tau śarair ācitau vīrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau petatur gaganād bhūmiṃ sūryācandramasāv iva
english: Those two heroic brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, covered with arrows, fell from the sky to the earth like the sun and moon fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tāv ubhau patitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarāv amitaujasau babandha rāvaṇir bhūyaḥ śarair dattavarais tadā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Seeing those two brothers of boundless might both fallen, the son of Rāvaṇa then again bound them with his boon-given arrows.

sanskrit: tau vīrau śarajālena baddhāv indrajitā raṇe rejatuḥ puruṣavyāghrau śakuntāv iva pañjare
english: Those two tiger-men, bound in battle by Indrajit in a net of arrows, lay there shining like two birds in a cage.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā patitau bhūmau śataśaḥ sāyakaiś citau sugrīvaḥ kapibhiḥ sārdhaṃ parivārya tataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Seeing those two fallen on the ground, covered with hundreds of arrows, Sugrīva stood there surrounding them together with the monkeys.

sanskrit: suṣeṇamaindadvividaiḥ kumudenāṅgadena ca hanūmannīlatāraiś ca nalena ca kapīśvaraḥ
english: The lord of monkeys stood there with Suṣeṇa, Mainda, Dvivida, Kumuda, Aṅgada, Hanūmān, Nīla, Tāra, and Nala.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ deśam āgamya kṛtakarmā vibhīṣaṇaḥ bodhayām āsa tau vīrau prajñāstreṇa prabodhitau
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, who had accomplished his task, came to that place and awakened those two heroes; they were revived by the weapon of wisdom.

sanskrit: viśalyau cāpi sugrīvaḥ kṣaṇenobhau cakāra tau viśalyayā mahauṣadhyā divyamantraprayuktayā
english: Sugrīva also rendered them both free of arrows in an instant, using the great herb Viśalyā, applied with divine incantations.

sanskrit: tau labdhasaṃjñau nṛvarau viśalyāv udatiṣṭhatām gatatandrīklamau cāstāṃ kṣaṇenobhau mahārathau
english: Those two best of men, having regained consciousness and freed of arrows, rose up; both great warriors were in an instant free of fatigue and exhaustion.

sanskrit: tato vibhīṣaṇaḥ pārtha rāmam ikṣvākunandanam uvāca vijvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāñjalir idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, O Pārtha, seeing Rāma the joy of the Ikṣvāku line free of fever, spoke these words with palms joined in reverence:

sanskrit: ayam ambho gṛhītvā tu rājarājasya śāsanāt guhyako 'bhyāgataḥ śvetāt tvatsakāśam ariṃdama
english: "This water has been brought: by order of the king of kings, a Guhyaka has come from Mount Śveta to your presence, O subduer of enemies."

sanskrit: idam ambhaḥ kuberas te mahārājaḥ prayacchati antarhitānāṃ bhūtānāṃ darśanārthaṃ paraṃtapa
english: "This water, O scorcher of foes, the great king Kubera offers to you, so that you may behold beings that are hidden from sight."

sanskrit: anena spṛṣṭanayano bhūtāny antarhitāny uta bhavān drakṣyati yasmai ca bhavān etat pradāsyati
english: "One whose eyes are touched by this will see beings that are hidden; and so too will anyone to whom you give it."

sanskrit: tatheti rāmas tad vāri pratigṛhyātha satkṛtam cakāra netrayoḥ śaucaṃ lakṣmaṇaś ca mahāmanāḥ
english: Saying "So be it," Rāma received that water with due honour and purified his eyes with it; and the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa did likewise.

sanskrit: sugrīvajāmbavantau ca hanūmān aṅgadas tathā maindadvividanīlāś ca prāyaḥ plavagasattamāḥ
english: Sugrīva and Jāmbavān, Hanūmān, Aṅgada, Mainda, Dvivida, Nīla — all the foremost among the monkeys did the same.

sanskrit: tathā samabhavac cāpi yad uvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇenātīndriyāṇy eṣāṃ cakṣūṃṣy āsan yudhiṣṭhira
english: And it came to pass just as Vibhīṣaṇa had said: in an instant, O Yudhiṣṭhira, their eyes became capable of perceiving the supersensible.

sanskrit: indrajit kṛtakarmā tu pitre karma tadātmanaḥ nivedya punar āgacchat tvarayājiśiraḥ prati
english: But Indrajit, having accomplished his deed, reported his exploit to his father and then came back swiftly toward the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ punar eva yuyutsayā abhidudrāva saumitrir vibhīṣaṇamate sthitaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa, acting on Vibhīṣaṇa's counsel, rushed forward against him as he came charging in fury once more with desire for battle.

sanskrit: akṛtāhnikam evainaṃ jighāṃsur jitakāśinam śarair jaghāna saṃkruddhaḥ kṛtasaṃjño 'tha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa, fully alert, in great fury, wishing to slay him before he could perform his daily rites, struck with arrows that one who bore the air of a conqueror.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tadānyonyaṃ jigīṣatoḥ atīva citram āścaryaṃ śakraprahlādayor iva
english: A battle arose between those two, each striving to conquer the other, exceedingly marvellous and wonderful, like the combat of Śakra and Prahlāda.

sanskrit: avidhyad indrajit tīkṣṇaiḥ saumitriṃ marmabhedibhiḥ saumitriś cānalasparśair avidhyad rāvaṇiṃ śaraiḥ
english: Indrajit pierced the son of Sumitrā with sharp arrows that struck the vital points; and the son of Sumitrā pierced the son of Rāvaṇa with arrows that burned like fire.

sanskrit: saumitriśarasaṃsparśād rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ asṛjal lakṣmaṇāyāṣṭau śarān āśīviṣopamān
english: Maddened with rage from the touch of the son of Sumitrā's arrows, the son of Rāvaṇa released eight shafts at Lakṣmaṇa, each comparable to a venomous serpent.

sanskrit: tasyāsūn pāvakasparśaiḥ saumitriḥ patribhis tribhiḥ yathā niraharad vīras tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: How that hero, the son of Sumitrā, drew out his vital breaths with three feathered arrows whose touch was like fire — hear me as I tell it.

sanskrit: ekenāsya dhanuṣmantaṃ bāhuṃ dehād apātayat dvitīyena sanārācaṃ bhujaṃ bhūmau nyapātayat
english: With one arrow he severed the bow-bearing arm from his body; with a second he sent to the ground the arm along with its iron-shafted arrows.

sanskrit: tṛtīyena tu bāṇena pṛthudhāreṇa bhāsvatā jahāra sunasaṃ cāru śiro bhrājiṣṇukuṇḍalam
english: With a third arrow, broad-bladed and blazing, he severed the handsome head with its bright-gleaming earrings and well-shaped nose.

sanskrit: vinikṛttabhujaskandhaṃ kabandhaṃ bhīmadarśanam taṃ hatvā sūtam apy astrair jaghāna balināṃ varaḥ
english: Having slain that headless trunk with its arms and shoulders cut off — terrible to behold — that best of the mighty then slew the charioteer too with his weapons.

sanskrit: laṅkāṃ praveśayām āsur vājinas taṃ rathaṃ tadā dadarśa rāvaṇas taṃ ca rathaṃ putravinākṛtam
english: The horses then drove the chariot into Laṅkā; and Rāvaṇa saw that chariot bereft of his son.

sanskrit: sa putraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā trāsāt saṃbhrāntalocanaḥ rāvaṇaḥ śokamohārto vaidehīṃ hantum udyataḥ
english: Seeing his son slain, Rāvaṇa, his eyes bewildered with terror, overwhelmed by grief and delusion, rose up with intent to kill the daughter of Videha.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāsthāṃ tāṃ rāmadarśanalālasām khaḍgam ādāya duṣṭātmā javenābhipapāta ha
english: That evil-souled one seized his sword and rushed swiftly upon her who dwelt in the Aśoka grove, longing to behold Rāma.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya durbuddher avindhyaḥ pāpaniścayam śamayām āsa saṃkruddhaṃ śrūyatāṃ yena hetunā
english: Seeing that wicked resolve of the evil-minded one, Avindhya appeased his fury — hear by what reasoning.

sanskrit: mahārājye sthito dīpte na striyaṃ hantum arhasi hataivaiṣā yadā strī ca bandhanasthā ca te gṛhe
english: "Established in your blazing great sovereignty, you ought not to slay a woman. She is as good as already slain — she is a woman and imprisoned in your house."

sanskrit: na caiṣā dehabhedena hatā syād iti me matiḥ jahi bhartāram evāsyā hate tasmin hatā bhavet
english: "It is my view that she should not be killed by destroying her body. Kill her husband instead; when he is slain, she will be slain."

sanskrit: na hi te vikrame tulyaḥ sākṣād api śatakratuḥ asakṛd dhi tvayā sendrās trāsitās tridaśā yudhi
english: "For none equals you in valour, not even the hundred-sacrificed Indra himself — it was you who more than once drove the gods together with Indra to terror in battle."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhair vākyair avindhyo rāvaṇaṃ tadā kruddhaṃ saṃśamayām āsa jagṛhe ca sa tadvacaḥ
english: With such diverse arguments Avindhya then pacified the enraged Rāvaṇa, and Rāvaṇa took those words to heart.

sanskrit: niryāṇe sa matiṃ kṛtvā nidhāyāsiṃ kṣapācaraḥ ājñāpayām āsa tadā ratho me kalpyatām iti
english: Having made up his mind to march out, that night-roamer laid aside his sword and commanded: "Let my chariot be made ready."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ priye putre nipātite niryayau ratham āsthāya hemaratnavibhūṣitam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then the ten-necked Rāvaṇa, furious at the fall of his beloved son, marched out riding a chariot adorned with gold and jewels.

sanskrit: saṃvṛto rākṣasair ghorair vividhāyudhapāṇibhiḥ abhidudrāva rāmaṃ sa pothayan hariyūthapān
english: Surrounded by terrible rakshasas bearing various weapons in their hands, he charged toward Rāma, crushing the leaders of the monkey troops.

sanskrit: tam ādravantaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ maindanīlanalāṅgadāḥ hanūmāñ jāmbavāṃś caiva sasainyāḥ paryavārayan
english: Mainda, Nīla, Nala, Aṅgada, Hanūmān, and Jāmbavān, together with their forces, surrounded him as he charged in fury.

sanskrit: te daśagrīvasainyaṃ tad ṛkṣavānarayūthapāḥ drumair vidhvaṃsayāṃ cakrur daśagrīvasya paśyataḥ
english: Those leaders of bear and monkey troops shattered Rāvaṇa's army with trees, as Rāvaṇa watched.

sanskrit: tataḥ svasainyam ālokya vadhyamānam arātibhiḥ māyāvī vyadadhān māyāṃ rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: Then, seeing his own army being slaughtered by the foes, Rāvaṇa the lord of rakshasas, master of illusion, deployed his illusion.

sanskrit: tasya dehād viniṣkrāntāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ rākṣasāḥ pratyadṛśyanta śaraśaktyṛṣṭipāṇayaḥ
english: Hundreds and thousands of rakshasas issued forth from his body and became visible, holding arrows, spears, and javelins in their hands.

sanskrit: tān rāmo jaghnivān sarvān divyenāstreṇa rākṣasān atha bhūyo 'pi māyāṃ sa vyadadhād rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Rāma slew all those rakshasas with his divine weapon; but then the lord of rakshasas deployed yet another illusion.

sanskrit: kṛtvā rāmasya rūpāṇi lakṣmaṇasya ca bhārata abhidudrāva rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ ca daśānanaḥ
english: Assuming the forms of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, O Bhārata, the ten-faced one charged toward both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tatas te rāmam archanto lakṣmaṇaṃ ca kṣapācarāḥ abhipetus tadā rājan pragṛhītoccakārmukāḥ
english: Then those night-wanderers, assailing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with those forms, advanced upon them, O king, with bows drawn high.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasendrasya māyām ikṣvākunandanaḥ uvāca rāmaṃ saumitrir asaṃbhrānto bṛhad vacaḥ
english: Seeing that illusion of the lord of rakshasas, Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, the delight of the Ikṣvākus, unperturbed, spoke these bold words to Rāma:

sanskrit: jahīmān rākṣasān pāpān ātmanaḥ pratirūpakān jaghāna rāmas tāṃś cānyān ātmanaḥ pratirūpakān
english: "Slay these evil rakshasas who have assumed your likeness!" And Rāma slew those and others who had taken on his likeness.

sanskrit: tato haryaśvayuktena rathenādityavarcasā upatasthe raṇe rāmaṃ mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ
english: Then Mātali, charioteer of Indra, came up to Rāma on the battlefield in a chariot yoked with tawny horses and blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: mātalir uvāca ayaṃ haryaśvayug jaitro maghonaḥ syandanottamaḥ anena śakraḥ kākutstha samare daityadānavān śataśaḥ puruṣavyāghra rathodāreṇa jaghnivān
english: Mātali said: "This is the victorious, best of chariots of Indra, yoked with tawny horses. With this noble chariot, O Kākutstha, O tiger of men, Indra slew the Daityas and Dānavas by the hundreds in battle."

sanskrit: tad anena naravyāghra mayā yat tena saṃyuge syandanena jahi kṣipraṃ rāvaṇaṃ mā ciraṃ kṛthāḥ
english: "Therefore, O tiger of men, mount this chariot brought by me — the same one — and swiftly slay Rāvaṇa; do not delay."

sanskrit: ity ukto rāghavas tathyaṃ vaco 'śaṅkata mātaleḥ māyeyaṃ rākṣasasyeti tam uvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the Rāghava doubted the truth of Mātali's words — thinking: "This may be the demon's illusion" — and Vibhīṣaṇa said to him:

sanskrit: neyaṃ māyā naravyāghra rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ tad ātiṣṭha rathaṃ śīghram imam aindraṃ mahādyute
english: "This is not the illusion of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, O tiger of men. Therefore mount this chariot of Indra quickly, O greatly resplendent one."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ kākutsthas tathety uktvā vibhīṣaṇam rathenābhipapātāśu daśagrīvaṃ ruṣānvitaḥ
english: Then the Kākutstha, greatly delighted, saying "So be it" to Vibhīṣaṇa, swiftly charged upon the ten-necked Rāvaṇa with that chariot, filled with fury.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtāni bhūtāni rāvaṇe samabhidrute siṃhanādāḥ sapaṭahā divi divyāś ca nānadan
english: As Rāvaṇa was charged upon, cries of "Alas! Alas!" arose from all beings; lion-roars with kettle-drums resounded in the sky, and divine sounds rang out.

sanskrit: sa rāmāya mahāghoraṃ visasarja niśācaraḥ śūlam indrāśaniprakhyaṃ brahmadaṇḍam ivodyatam
english: That night-wanderer hurled at Rāma a most terrible trident, comparable to Indra's thunderbolt, like the rod of Brahmā raised aloft.
